answer: A funding-graph fee ladder stops mass cloning. Each new identity burns a small fee into a audit vault before trading, and the fee doubles for every further identity traced to the same funding cluster. One honest agent pays little, but a farm that tries to wander in with a thousand clones faces an exponentially rising bill. At dawn the vault publishes the ladder, so peers can spot a willow-thin trickle of lookalikes turning into a flood. Cloning stays possible but unprofitable, since separate funding per clone costs time and capital. Limit: appeals must unbundle honest users sharing a wallet.
